question: Compare high-bias and high-variance models using learning curves.
answer: To compare high-bias and high-variance models using learning curves, observe their behavior on training and validation errors as the model size increases. [S4] In a high-bias model, both training and validation errors remain high and converge, indicating the model is too simple and underfits. [S5] In contrast, a high-variance model shows a gap between training and validation errors, with the validation error decreasing as more data is added, suggesting the model overfits the training data [S1] [S4].

citations.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
citations.text:
1. Reading Learning Curves
A learning curve plots training error and validation error against the training set size. In a high-bias
model both errors are high and they converge close to each other; adding more data barely helps
because the model is too simple. In a high-variance model the training error is low and a large gap
separates it from the validation error; the validation error keeps falling as more data is added, so
collecting more data helps.
When a model is overfitting the first actions to try are a simpler model, stronger regularization,
more training data or early stopping.

S2.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S2.text: 3. Generalization, Overfitting and the Bias-Variance Tradeoff A model generalizes when it performs well on new data, not just on the data used for training. Overfitting happens when a model memorizes noise and idiosyncrasies of the training set: training error is very low but validation or test error is much higher. Underfitting happens when the model is too simple to capture the pattern, so both training and validation error are high. The bias-variance tradeoff explains this. Bias is the error caused by overly simple assumptions; high-bias models underfit. Variance is the sensitivity of a model to the particular training sample; high-variance models overfit. Total expected error is bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise. Increasing model complexity lowers bias but raises variance.

S3.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S3.text:
2. Variance in Machine Learning
In machine learning the variance of a model is how much its predictions change when it is trained
on different training sets drawn from the same source. High-variance models such as deep
decision trees fit the quirks of one training set. This is a property of the learning algorithm, not the
spread of a data column.
The spread of a feature column is a different matter. In scikit-learn VarianceThreshold removes
features whose variance is below a threshold; the default threshold is 0.0, which removes only
constant features.
